headline: Warren Buffett Steps Down as Berkshire Chairman; Howard Buffett Takes Role
seoTitle: Warren Buffett Becomes Berkshire Chairman Emeritus; Howard Buffett Elected Chairman | FMB News
seoDescription: Berkshire Hathaway says Warren Buffett has become chairman emeritus while remaining a director, with Howard G. Buffett elected chairman under the company's succession plan.
deck: Berkshire Hathaway says the change is effective immediately. Warren Buffett remains on the board, while CEO Greg Abel continues to run the company and Howard G. Buffett becomes chairman.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Berkshire Hathaway announced that Warren E. Buffett has become chairman emeritus, effective immediately, completing another stage of the conglomerate's long-planned leadership transition.
The board elected Howard G. Buffett, Warren Buffett's son and a Berkshire director since 1993, as chairman. Susan L. Decker remains lead independent director.

sections.heading: What is confirmed
paragraphs: Warren Buffett is not leaving Berkshire's board. The company says he will remain a director and continue to offer his judgment and perspective.
Greg Abel remains Berkshire's chief executive officer. The chairman transition therefore does not transfer day-to-day executive control from Abel to Howard Buffett.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: Warren Buffett built Berkshire from its textile-company origins into a conglomerate spanning insurance, rail, energy, manufacturing, retail and a large public-equity portfolio. He had already handed the chief executive role to Abel before this latest board transition.
Howard Buffett's chairmanship follows Berkshire's previously described succession structure, in which the chairman role and chief executive role are held separately.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: The change formally ends Warren Buffett's decades as Berkshire chairman while preserving his board role. It also puts the company's planned post-Buffett governance structure into operation, with Abel responsible for management and Howard Buffett chairing the board.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Investors will watch how Berkshire's board oversight, capital allocation and corporate culture evolve under the split leadership of Abel as CEO and Howard Buffett as chairman. Warren Buffett's chairman-emeritus title does not itself define how often he will participate in future decisions.

verificationNotes: Berkshire Hathaway's September 18 official release states that Warren Buffett became chairman emeritus effective immediately, remains a director, and that the board elected Howard G. Buffett chairman.
Reuters independently reported the leadership change and confirmed that Warren Buffett remains on the board.
The Washington Post independently reported the transition and the continued CEO role of Greg Abel.
The article distinguishes the non-executive chairman transition from day-to-day management under CEO Greg Abel and does not imply Warren Buffett has left Berkshire entirely.
